questions.text:
Tuatara have lived in Aotearoa New Zealand for around 60 million years. The earliest ferns found in New Zealand date back roughly 300 million years.

The timeline below runs from 300 million years ago (earliest ferns) to today, with five arrows labelled 1 to 5 at equal intervals (each interval is 50 million years).

A scientist wants to mark when dinosaurs first appeared (about 240 million years ago). Which numbered arrow is closest to 240 million years ago?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Each arrow is 50 million years apart, working forward from 300 mya.

Step 2: Arrow 1 = 250 mya, Arrow 2 = 200 mya, Arrow 3 = 150 mya, Arrow 4 = 100 mya, Arrow 5 = 50 mya.

Step 3: 240 mya: distance to Arrow 1 (250) = 10, distance to Arrow 2 (200) = 40.

Step 4: Closest is Arrow 1.

Final answer: 1.

questions.text:
An adult kererū (wood pigeon) weighs 650 grams. A young kererū chick weighs only 1/10 of the adult's weight, and the largest karaka berry it eats weighs 13 grams.

How many of these karaka berries together would have the SAME mass as the chick?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Chick mass = 1/10 of 650 g = 65 g.

Step 2: Number of berries = 65 ÷ 13 = 5.

Step 3: So 5 berries together weigh the same as the chick.

questions.text:
A pair of tui nests TWICE each year. Each nest produces between 2 and 4 chicks, but only about HALF of all chicks survive to leave the nest.

Using the AVERAGE number of chicks per nest (3), estimate how many surviving chicks one pair of tui would produce in 6 years. Show your working.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Average chicks per nest = 3.

Step 2: Chicks per year = 2 nests × 3 chicks = 6 chicks.

Step 3: Over 6 years = 6 × 6 = 36 chicks.

Step 4: Half survive: 36 ÷ 2 = 18 surviving chicks.

Step 5: Student must show all working steps. Accept answers between 12 and 24 if working clearly justifies the figure.

Final answer: 18 surviving chicks.

questions.text:
In 2010, a conservation group planted native trees on a reserve. The graph above shows how many trees were alive each year.

(a) Calculate the average number of NEW trees added per year between 2012 and 2018.
(b) Between which TWO consecutive listed years did the trees increase by the largest NUMBER? Give your final answer as the average from part (a) only.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Read from the graph: 2012 = 40 trees, 2018 = 160 trees.

Step 2: Increase = 160 − 40 = 120 trees over 6 years.

Step 3: Average per year = 120 ÷ 6 = 20 trees per year.

Step 4: For (b), the intervals are 2012→2014: +30, 2014→2016: +40, 2016→2018: +50 — the largest jump is between 2016 and 2018 (+50 trees).

Final answer (numeric): 20.

questions.text:
Volunteers measured the heights of 25 young kauri trees. The histogram above shows the distribution. The median height is 1.4 m.

A volunteer says: 'Most of the trees are taller than the median.'

Using data from the histogram, explain whether this statement is correct AND identify what the median actually tells you about a data set.
questions.expectedAnswer: Incorrect — by definition the median splits the data so that about HALF the trees are above and HALF are below the median. From the histogram, 12 trees are below 1.4 m and 13 are at/above, so the volunteer is wrong.
questions.markingGuide:
Student must show that they understand the median is the middle value (not the average).

From the data: bars below 1.4 m are 0.5–0.8 (3), 0.8–1.1 (4), 1.1–1.4 (5) = 12 trees.

Bars at/above 1.4 m are 1.4–1.7 (7), 1.7–2.0 (4), 2.0–2.2 (2) = 13 trees.

12 vs 13 is essentially half/half — so the claim 'most are taller' is false.

Must also state the median is the MIDDLE value of an ordered data set (about 50% above, 50% below).

questions.text:
A nature reserve is approximately 150 km south of Hamilton on a straight bearing. A school group plans to drive there at an average speed of 75 km/h.

Which town listed below is closest to the reserve, AND approximately how long will the drive take?

(A) Tauranga (about 105 km east of Hamilton)
(B) Taupō (about 150 km south of Hamilton)
(C) New Plymouth (about 200 km south-west of Hamilton)
(D) Rotorua (about 110 km south-east of Hamilton)
(E) Whanganui (about 260 km south-west of Hamilton)
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: The reserve is 150 km south of Hamilton — Taupō is the closest match (B).

Step 2: Time = distance ÷ speed = 150 ÷ 75 = 2 hours.

Step 3: Accept B.

questions.text:
Wiremu creates a growing triangle pattern using toothpicks.

Pattern 1: 3 toothpicks. Pattern 2: 9. Pattern 3: 19. Pattern 4: 33. The differences between consecutive patterns are 6, 10, 14 (each difference increases by 4).

How many toothpicks would Pattern 6 need IN TOTAL?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: The differences are: 6, 10, 14, ... each increases by 4.

Step 2: Next differences after 14 are 18, then 22.

Step 3: Pattern 5 = 33 + 18 = 51.

Step 4: Pattern 6 = 51 + 22 = 73.

Step 5: Final answer: 73 toothpicks.

questions.text:
Hana is designing a woven mat with 12 numbered horizontal stripes (1–12). The pattern repeats every 3 stripes, and each repeating block has ONE line of reflection symmetry through its middle stripe.

Which numbered stripes are lines of reflection symmetry across the WHOLE mat? Select ALL that apply.
questions.markingGuide:
The pattern repeats every 3 stripes, so the blocks are stripes 1–3, 4–6, 7–9, 10–12.

The middle of each block is stripes 2, 5, 8, 11.

These are the lines of reflection symmetry.

questions.text:
Standard cartoon proportions say the head is 1/4 of the total figure height, the legs start at 1/2, and the arms reach down to 5/8 of the total height.

A student's drawing has the legs starting at 2/5 of the height. By what FRACTION of the total height are the legs drawn TOO HIGH?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Convert to a common denominator: 1/2 = 5/10 and 2/5 = 4/10.

Step 2: Difference = 5/10 − 4/10 = 1/10.

Step 3: The legs are drawn 1/10 of the figure's total height too high.

Final answer: 1/10.

questions.text:
A trophy is shaped like a cylinder (the base) with a square-based pyramid (the top) sitting on it. The cylinder has diameter 10 cm and the pyramid's base is a square that just fits inside the top of the cylinder.

Viewed FROM ABOVE (top view), what shape would you see?
options: A circle with a square inscribed inside it (the square's corners touching the circle)
questions.expectedAnswer: A circle with a square inscribed inside it (the square's corners touching the circle)
questions.markingGuide:
Looking from directly above, you see the circular outline of the cylinder PLUS the square outline of the pyramid base sitting inside the circle (its corners touching the circle).

The pyramid itself appears as a square because you are looking straight down its central axis.

Accept the option that mentions both circle AND inscribed square.

questions.text:
In 1990, a rare NZ coin sold for $400. In 2024, it sold for $2 million.

(a) How many TIMES more valuable is the coin in 2024 than 1990?
(b) By what PERCENTAGE has the value increased? Tick the closest answer.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: $2,000,000 ÷ $400 = 5,000. So the coin is 5,000 times more valuable.

Step 2: Increase = $2,000,000 − $400 = $1,999,600.

Step 3: Percentage increase = (1,999,600 ÷ 400) × 100 = 4,999 × 100 = 499,900%.

Step 4: Accept the option '5,000 times more, 499,900% increase'.

questions.text:
A bus drives from Auckland to Rotorua. The driver records the trip as 3 hours 42 minutes of driving and TWO breaks of 18 minutes each.

What is the TOTAL time from Auckland to Rotorua, rounded to the nearest 15 minutes? Give your answer in hours and minutes.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Driving = 3 h 42 min.

Step 2: Break time = 2 × 18 = 36 min.

Step 3: Total = 3 h 42 min + 36 min = 4 h 18 min.

Step 4: Round to nearest 15 minutes: 18 min is closer to 15 min than to 30 min, so round to 4 h 15 min.

Final answer: 4 hours 15 minutes.

questions.text:
A large fish tank holds 18 litres of water when full and weighs 18.45 kilograms when full.

(One litre of water weighs one kilogram.)

How much does the EMPTY tank weigh, in GRAMS?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: 18 L of water weighs 18 kg.

Step 2: Empty tank = 18.45 − 18.00 = 0.45 kg.

Step 3: Convert to grams: 0.45 × 1000 = 450 g.

Final answer: 450.

questions.text:
Six bottles each hold 1.25 litres of cordial. The cordial must be diluted with water in the ratio 1 part cordial to 4 parts water before serving.

How many 250 mL cups of DILUTED drink can be made from all six bottles?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Total cordial = 6 × 1.25 = 7.5 L = 7,500 mL.

Step 2: Ratio is 1 cordial : 4 water, so total drink is 5 parts (1 + 4).

Step 3: Total diluted drink = 7,500 × 5 = 37,500 mL.

Step 4: Number of 250 mL cups = 37,500 ÷ 250 = 150.

Final answer: 150.

questions.text:
Water makes up about 55% of an adult dog's body weight and about 75% of a puppy's body weight. The puppy weighs 4 kg and the adult dog weighs 8 kg.

The owner wants to give each dog a daily 'water from food' contribution equal to 10% of the dog's water weight.

How much water (in grams) does the OWNER need to provide for BOTH dogs combined?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Puppy water = 75% of 4 kg = 3 kg.

Step 2: Adult dog water = 55% of 8 kg = 4.4 kg.

Step 3: Total water in both dogs = 3 + 4.4 = 7.4 kg.

Step 4: 10% of 7.4 kg = 0.74 kg.

Step 5: Convert to grams: 0.74 × 1000 = 740 g.

Final answer: 740.

questions.text:
Tama's internet bill says he used 240 GB of data and was charged $72.00, plus a fixed monthly access fee of $30.00 (the $72.00 does NOT include the access fee).

What is Tama's TOTAL bill, AND what is the average cost per GB of data when the access fee is included?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Total bill = $72.00 + $30.00 = $102.00.

Step 2: Average cost per GB = $102.00 ÷ 240 = $0.425 per GB.

Step 3: Accept 0.425 (or $0.43 rounded to nearest cent — both should be marked correct with working).

Final answer: 0.425.

questions.text:
Mere's whānau of four people want to save water. The table above shows their current daily water use.

Mere has two ideas:
• Idea 1: Reduce shower time from 8 minutes to 4 minutes per person (each shower).
• Idea 2: Run the washing machine every 2 days instead of every day.

(a) Calculate the daily water saving in LITRES from EACH idea (assume each person showers once per day).
(b) State which idea saves more water and by how much per WEEK (7 days).
questions.expectedAnswer: Idea 1 saves 100 L more per day; over a week that is 700 L more
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Idea 1: shower saving per person = 80 − 40 = 40 L. For 4 people = 160 L/day.

Step 2: Idea 2: washing machine — saves 120 L every 2 days = 60 L/day on average.

Step 3: Difference = 160 − 60 = 100 L/day in favour of Idea 1.

Step 4: Per week = 100 × 7 = 700 L.

Final answer: Idea 1 saves 100 L per day more than Idea 2, which is 700 L more per week.

questions.text:
The chart above shows the average sunshine hours each month in Dunedin.

Calculate the AVERAGE monthly sunshine across the three SUMMER months (Dec, Jan, Feb), AND determine how many MORE hours of sunshine the average summer month has compared to the average WINTER month (Jun, Jul, Aug). Give the difference (in whole hours).
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Summer total = Dec 185 + Jan 190 + Feb 165 = 540. Summer average = 540 ÷ 3 = 180 hours.

Step 2: Winter total = Jun 80 + Jul 90 + Aug 110 = 280. Winter average = 280 ÷ 3 ≈ 93.33 hours.

Step 3: Difference = 180 − 93.33 ≈ 86.67 hours.

Step 4: Rounded to whole hours = 87.

Final answer: 87.

questions.text:
Pasifika Festival is held annually in Auckland. The chart above shows attendance.

(There was no event in 2020 or 2021 due to COVID-19.)

Calculate the PERCENTAGE INCREASE in attendance from 2015 to 2022. Give your answer to the nearest whole percent.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: 2015 attendance = 25,000. 2022 attendance = 65,000.

Step 2: Increase = 65,000 − 25,000 = 40,000.

Step 3: Percentage increase = (40,000 ÷ 25,000) × 100 = 1.6 × 100 = 160%.

Step 4: Accept 160.

Final answer: 160.

questions.text:
Pasifika Festival organisers think attendance will reach 85,000 by 2026.

Using the data, calculate the AVERAGE yearly increase between 2015 and 2018, then explain whether the 85,000 target by 2026 is REASONABLE based on that rate. (Assume attendance also grew at this average rate from 2018 to 2026.)
questions.expectedAnswer: Average yearly increase 2015–2018 was about 8,333 per year. At that rate from 2018 (50,000), 8 more years would add 66,667, giving roughly 116,667. So 85,000 is well within reach — the target is reasonable, possibly conservative.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: 2015 = 25,000, 2018 = 50,000. Increase = 25,000 over 3 years.

Step 2: Average yearly increase = 25,000 ÷ 3 ≈ 8,333.

Step 3: From 2018 to 2026 is 8 years. 8 × 8,333 = 66,667.

Step 4: Predicted 2026 attendance = 50,000 + 66,667 ≈ 116,667.

Step 5: Conclusion: 85,000 is well within this trend, so the target is reasonable (perhaps conservative).

Accept any answer that uses the rate calculation correctly and reaches a justified conclusion.

Final answer: Yes, reasonable — at the historic average rate, attendance could exceed 85,000 by 2026.

questions.text:
Ticket prices for a school cultural showcase are:
• $6.00 — Standard (online, fixed night)
• $8.00 — Flexi (online, any night)
• $10.00 — Door entry on the night

If you buy Standard tickets online for two nights, you get a 25% discount off the total. A 15% booking fee is then added to the discounted price.

Three adults want to attend on both Friday and Saturday using the Standard option.

What is the TOTAL cost for the group (in dollars to the nearest cent)?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: 3 adults × $6.00 × 2 nights = $36.00 (full price).

Step 2: Apply 25% discount: $36.00 × 0.75 = $27.00.

Step 3: Apply 15% booking fee: $27.00 × 1.15 = $31.05.

Step 4: Final total = $31.05.

Final answer: 31.05.

questions.text:
A school fun run has 12 competing teams from different zones. The pie chart above shows how many teams come from each zone.

If each team has an equal chance of winning, what is the probability that the winner comes from the EAST or WEST zone? Give your answer as a SIMPLIFIED fraction.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: East = 2 teams, West = 1 team.

Step 2: East or West = 3 teams out of 12.

Step 3: Probability = 3/12 = 1/4.

Final answer: 1/4 (or 0.25).

questions.text:
The timetable above shows the morning rugby and netball games at a school sports day.

Calculate the TOTAL minutes of GAME time (rugby + netball, NOT counting breaks) shown in the morning timetable.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Rugby — 3 games of 25 minutes each = 75 minutes.

Step 2: Netball — 4 games of 15 minutes each = 60 minutes.

Step 3: Total game time = 75 + 60 = 135 minutes.

Final answer: 135.

questions.text:
A marching group performs a routine on a rectangular field that measures 30 m by 20 m. They want to add a triangular performance zone in front of the rectangle. The triangle has the same 30 m base as the rectangle and a height of 8 m.

Calculate the TOTAL AREA of the marching display (rectangle + triangle), in square metres.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Rectangle area = 30 × 20 = 600 m².

Step 2: Triangle area = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 30 × 8 = 120 m².

Step 3: Total area = 600 + 120 = 720 m².

Final answer: 720.
